# Gradient scale in column {#sec-table-column-fill}



```{r}

basic_table <- veg_summarized |>
  filter(!is.na(sd_d)) |>
  gt(process_md = T) |>
  # replace default NA values with a "-"
  # Note: modifying the data with {dplyr} functions would work equally well but {gt} has a devoted function for this purpose
  sub_missing(columns = "sd_d", missing_text = "-") |>
  tab_style(
    style = list(
      cell_text(style = "italic")
    ),
    # family names in italics
    locations = cells_body(columns = "family")
  ) |>
  # ^13^ is markdown for superscript, &delta is html for lower case Greek delta
  tab_spanner(columns = contains("_d"), label = md("&delta;^13^C")) |>
  cols_label(
    family = "Family",
    country = "Country",
    type = "Type",
    n_plants = "Observations",
    mean_d = "Mean",
    sd_d = "SD"
  ) |>
  fmt_markdown(columns = c("type")) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c("mean_d", "sd_d"), decimals = 2)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

basic_table
```


There are many great resources related to colours and colour palettes (e.g., [Color Palette Finder](https://r-graph-gallery.com/color-palette-finder) by Yan Holtz, or NR XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX). For the sake of this tutorial, we will use HCL palettes from the `{grDevices}`. There are over 110 qualitative, sequentinal and diverging palettes in this collection. ([HCL-Based Color Palettes](https://colorspace.r-forge.r-project.org/articles/hcl_palettes.html)).


## Continous variables

```{r}
#| warning: true

preformat_tbl <- basic_table |> 
  # per-column cell fill
  data_color(n_plants,
             method = "numeric",
             palette = "BurgYl")
```


**Observation counts**

```{r}
preformat_tbl <- basic_table |> 
  # per-column cell fill
  data_color(n_plants,
             method = "numeric",
             palette = rev(hcl.colors(2, palette = "BurgYl")))
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

preformat_tbl
```


**Mean δ^13^C and SD**

```{r}
cont_table <- preformat_tbl |> 
  data_color(c("mean_d", "sd_d"),
             method = "numeric",
             palette = "Greens")
```


```{r}
#| echo: false

cont_table
```


## Discrete variables

```{r}
basic_table |> 
  data_color(c("type"),
             method = "factor",
             palette = c("#FDC718FF", "#3E938BFF"))
```

## Including a legend

Make dummy plot

```{r}
dummy_df <- data.frame(x = c("A", "B", "C"),
                       y = c(1, 2, 3),
                       fill_value = c(1, 50, 100))

dummy_plot <- ggplot(dummy_df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = fill_value)) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colors = rev(hcl.colors(2, "Greens")),
                       breaks = c(1, 100), labels = c("min", "max")) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title = element_blank(),
        legend.ticks = element_blank())

dummy_plot
```
and export only legend `{ggpubr}`

```{r}
library(ggpubr)
```


```{r}
fill_legend <- as_ggplot(get_legend(dummy_plot))
```


```{r}
dummy_fxn <- function(){
  dummy_plot <- ggplot(dummy_df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = fill_value)) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(colors = rev(hcl.colors(2, "Greens")),
                         breaks = c(1, 100), labels = c("min", "max")) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.title = element_blank(),
          legend.ticks = element_blank(),
          legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
          legend.key.height = unit(120, "pt"),
          legend.key.width = unit(225, "pt"),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 70),
          plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
  
  fill_legend <- as_ggplot(get_legend(dummy_plot))
  
  return(fill_legend)
}
```


```{r}
cont_table |> 
  tab_footnote(footnote = html(glue::glue(
      "<div style='float: left; top: 100%; bottom: 0%; transform: translate(0%, -105); margin-left: -15%;'>
         {dummy_fxn() |> ggplot_image(height = 50, aspect_ratio = 6)}
       </div>"
    )))
```
